clue.text: Saddle with a non-alcoholic drink

parts.note: a col is a saddle, the dip in a ridge between two mountain peaks

explanation.surface: Someone is lumbered with a soft drink when they wanted something stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saddle' looks like a verb (to burden) but it is the noun: a mountain saddle, or col.
explanation.definitionFit: A cola is a fizzy soft drink with no alcohol in it.

clue.text: Place where new car buyer keeps a collection of books

indicators.note: keeps means the rearranged letters hold the other piece inside them
new tells us the letters of the words car buyer are to be made over into a fresh order

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Somebody buying a new car also keeps a little library of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal and 'keeps' the container signal; NT for New Testament is a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Canterbury is a cathedral city in Kent, a place in south-east England.

clue.text: Grub that appears for the French painter about five

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

indicators.note: about means the painter's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A grub turns up in place of a French artist who is around five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; RA (Royal Academician) for a painter is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young feeding stage of an insect, and a grub is a beetle's larva.

clue.text: Let by the underworld — it's not to be tolerated !

indicators.note: by means placed next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and a name for the underworld itself
let means allowed, as in permitted

explanation.surface: Something permitted by the powers of hell turns out to be quite unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disallowed is refused or ruled out, so it is not to be permitted.

clue.text: Most ludicrous though popular article on bird sanctuary

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
article gives A
a nest is a bird's safe home, a sanctuary for it

explanation.surface: A trendy piece about a bird reserve is the silliest thing yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, so the superlative is the most foolish.

clue.text: The player getting caught in a lock of hair

indicators.note: getting caught in means the abbreviation for caught is set inside the other letters

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A performer gets snagged in a curl of someone's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting caught in' puts C inside A TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female performer, and a player is an actor on stage.

clue.text: A girl races into the meadow

indicators.note: into means the races are placed inside the meadow word

parts.note: a ley (or lea) is a meadow or grassland
the TT races are the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A young woman runs off into a grassy field.
explanation.definitionFit: Letty is a girl's name, a short form of Letitia.

clue.text: A reveller — one lamenting about dope

indicators.note: about means the mourner's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a wailer is someone who wails or laments
an ass is a dope, a fool

explanation.surface: Someone grieving over drugs is oddly described as a party-goer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'dope' looks like drugs in the surface but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wassailer is someone who goes wassailing, drinking and carousing at festivities.

clue.text: Expected money for a contest

parts.note: due means expected, as a train due at noon
L, for libra, is the abbreviation for pound, a sum of money

explanation.surface: Prize money that is owed for a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people, a contest of arms.

clue.text: Talks about permit reversing such effects

indicators.note: about means the talks word goes round the other piece

parts.note: chats are informal talks

indicators.note: reversing tells us the word for permit is read backwards

parts.note: to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Discussions about permission turn back the effects of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the permit word round and 'about' wraps the talks word around it; 'effects' means belongings, not results.
explanation.definitionFit: Effects are personal belongings, and chattels are movable possessions.

clue.text: A direction to make no threats

indicators.note: make means the letters of no threats are made into something new

explanation.surface: Advice on how to behave: never threaten anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: North-east is a compass bearing, one of the points between north and east.

clue.text: Sense discrimination

definitions.meaning: one of the five senses, the one using the tongue
the ability to judge what is fine or of quality

explanation.surface: Noticing differences is simply a matter of judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is both the sense of flavour on the tongue and refined judgment in matters of style.

clue.text: Right to insist upon

definitions.meaning: correct or precise in every detail
to demand something as a due, as with payment

explanation.surface: Someone has a right they intend to demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact is an adjective meaning precisely correct and a verb meaning to demand and obtain, as in levying a payment.

clue.text: The ordinary person among the very many weirdos

indicators.note: among means the letters are found within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Typical folk stand among a crowd of oddballs.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the words 'thE VERY MANy'; 'weirdos' is surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyman is the typical ordinary individual, named after the medieval morality play.

clue.text: Small, very small, the pictures may be, but dear

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
wee is Scots for tiny
art means pictures and paintings

explanation.surface: Tiny though the paintings are, they are costly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' looks like expensive, but it is the affectionate term for a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear is a term of endearment for a loved one, the same as a beloved.

clue.text: The most daring underclothing

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: The boldest underwear going.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravest is the superlative of brave, meaning most courageous.

clue.text: Moving praise about the favourite bonne bouche

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the other piece
moving means the letters of praise are shifted into another order

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as the teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Heartfelt compliments surround the best-loved tasty morsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' is the anagram signal, making APISER, and 'about' is the container signal; 'Moving' looks like 'touching' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonne bouche is a tasty morsel, especially one eaten before a meal to stimulate the palate.

clue.text: Consume a small bird

definitions.meaning: to eat or drink something down
a migratory bird with a forked tail

explanation.surface: Eat a little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallow means to gulp down food and is also the name of a fork-tailed migratory songbird.

clue.text: They feel for any six-footer

parts.note: a six-footer here is an insect with six legs, not a tall person, and these are its feelers

explanation.surface: Sympathy goes out to anyone very tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means an insect, and 'feel for' is literal: the organs it touches with.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae are the paired feelers on an insect's head used to sense its surroundings.

clue.text: Serving men, work over, take a rest — lay up

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are serving soldiers

indicators.note: over means the word for work is turned back to front

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
to sit is to take a rest

explanation.surface: Soldiers finish a job and then sit down for a breather.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposit is to store something away, the same as to lay it up for later.

clue.text: Do business — if craft is used

indicators.note: is used means the letters of if craft are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Trade is done if a vessel is put to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is used' signals that IFCRAFT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to trade or deal in goods, often illicitly.

clue.text: Set a little house beside a lake

indicators.note: beside means the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: a cot is a small cottage
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A small cottage by the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group, and a set is a social circle.

clue.text: Get rid of pollution and get rich!

definitions.meaning: to make a large profit quickly

explanation.surface: Removing contamination could make someone a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean up means both to remove dirt from somewhere and, informally, to make a big profit.

clue.text: Cod and skate management and protection

indicators.note: management means the fish names are handled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fish-stock control helps to look after cod and skate.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive barrier of upright stakes, built for protection.

clue.text: Material for credit record note

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an EP is an extended-play record
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Fabric that will earn credit for a recorded note.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a light fabric with a crinkled surface.

clue.text: Nick is not going to church

explanation.surface: Nick is skipping the Sunday service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name but is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut, and a notch is a V-shaped cut in an edge.

clue.text: Subject to ups and downs in the main

definitions.text: Subject to ups and downs in the main

parts.words: Subject to ups and downs in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea, whose level rises and falls twice a day

explanation.surface: Something that is mostly up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly', but 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidal describes water that rises and falls with the tides.

clue.text: A youngster showing a bit of leg

definitions.meaning: a young cow or other animal
the fleshy back part of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A child flashing a glimpse of leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf is both a young bovine and the muscular back of the human lower leg.

clue.text: Walk this way to become a union member !

definitions.text: Walk this way to become a union member !

parts.words: Walk this way to become a union member
parts.note: the union is marriage, and a bride walks up the church passage to the altar to wed

explanation.surface: Joining a trade union is just down this corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union member' suggests a trade union, but the union is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is the passage between church pews that a bride walks along.

clue.text: Arrange and fail in correctly naming music by Sibelius

indicators.note: arrange means the letters of and fail in are put in a different order

explanation.surface: An orchestra must arrange things and not miss naming a Sibelius piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Finlandia is a patriotic tone poem composed by Jean Sibelius in 1899.

clue.text: This offers a way out when things get too hot

definitions.text: This offers a way out when things get too hot

parts.words: This offers a way out when things get too hot
parts.note: too hot is literal here: a building on fire, not a tricky situation

explanation.surface: An excuse to slip away when life becomes difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too hot' reads as a figurative tight spot, but here it is a burning building.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire escape is an outside staircase for leaving a burning building.

clue.text: The stupid guy should be left in bed

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for left is placed inside the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: The fool ought to be left lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a fool or idiot.
